channel.title: AI Daily Watch: all topics
channel.description: Daily Microsoft, Copilot and AI news.

item.title: Microsoft details mobilezone’s deployment of three Copilot Studio agents
item.description: Microsoft and mobilezone: Microsoft reported that mobilezone built three Copilot Studio agents for store monitoring, sales order creation, and product creation. The store-monitoring agent helps a four-person IT support team query device information and investigate errors proactively, illustrating a live operational use of Copilot Studio agents.

item.title: Viva Glint previews Copilot Results Summarization for early November
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft announced a planned private preview of Results Summarization in Viva Glint Copilot Chat for early November. The experience brings survey scores and comment analysis together conversationally, with permissions and confidentiality safeguards continuing to apply.

item.title: Microsoft publishes its October 2026 security update release, including Windows updates
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft’s Security Update Guide lists its October 2026 security release as released on October 26 and includes cumulative updates for Windows. The release page reports 1,105 Windows vulnerabilities addressed and flags a Windows Shell security feature bypass vulnerability with exploitation detected.

item.title: Visual Studio adds resumable, unsaved Markdown investigation notes
item.description: Microsoft: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 can create standalone Markdown notes, and the opt-in Hot Exit preview can restore unsaved notes after Visual Studio is closed and reopened. This helps developers resume investigations without having to save the note or add it to a project first.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows weekly update highlights hardening and safer credential handling
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Agentic Workflows’ October 26 weekly update recaps six hardening releases, emphasizing stronger static analysis, safer credential handling, and clearer diagnostics. Highlighted changes include network credentials for safe-output integration jobs and secret-safe error diagnostics for engine-driver crashes.

item.title: OpenAI and Fanatics launch AI-powered Shop the Look
item.description: OpenAI: Fanatics launched Shop the Look, an OpenAI-powered feature that recommends coordinated, in-stock merchandise to sports fans. OpenAI says its team and Fanatics used Codex to develop recommendation tools, and testing across roughly 30,000 MLB products produced 10% higher engagement than the previous experience.

item.title: Google DeepMind and Springer Nature partner to develop an AI peer-review assistant
item.description: Google DeepMind and Springer Nature: Google DeepMind and Springer Nature announced a research partnership to co-design an AI assistant for peer reviewers. The prototype is intended to help researchers navigate manuscripts and analyze text, charts, and figures while keeping expert human judgment central.

item.title: Gemini API enables request storage by default for new paid-tier projects
item.description: Google: Starting October 26, new paid-tier projects using the Gemini Generate Content API store requests by default (`store=true`); existing projects retain their current setting. Developers can opt out by setting `store=false` per request or turning off API logging in AI Studio.

item.title: Meta plans up to $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta: Meta announced a plan to raise up to $95 billion through equity offerings to support its AI infrastructure and superintelligence investments. The plan combines an initial offering with a potential at-the-market program, underscoring the scale of capital required to expand AI computing capacity.

item.title: Oracle updates Private Agent Factory with Deep NL2SQL and expanded agent integration
item.description: Oracle: Oracle released version 26.10 of Private Agent Factory, adding Deep NL2SQL to let business users ask questions about enterprise data using maintained business context. The update also adds developer integration options, reusable knowledge ingestion, expanded agent-to-agent support, and observability, strengthening the platform’s enterprise-agent capabilities.

item.title: Anthropic publicly files S-1 registration statement for IPO
item.description: Anthropic: Anthropic publicly filed an S-1 registration statement, moving its planned IPO a step closer to a public offering. The filing provides investors with new details about the Claude maker’s business, including reported first-half 2026 revenue of $16.29 billion.

item.title: Microsoft introduces the Power Platform Admin plugin for Copilot Cowork
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft introduced the Power Platform Admin plugin for Copilot Cowork, letting IT administrators ask natural-language questions grounded in tenant-specific Power Platform data. The post describes using those findings to produce audience-specific summaries and governance reports.

item.title: Claude Code contributor Thariq says he has left Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic: Thariq publicly said he had left Anthropic after more than a year working on Claude Code. His post thanked colleagues and the Claude Code community; it is notable personnel news related to Claude Code, though it does not announce a product change.

item.title: Pennsylvania adopts disclosure labels for qualifying AI-generated ads
item.description: Pennsylvania: Pennsylvania enacted a law requiring labels on advertisements that are generated or significantly modified using AI, according to The Verge. The report notes that the law leaves some terms open to interpretation; the governor signed it on October 22, before the monitoring start date.

item.title: Study reports partisan differences in forced candidate recommendations by Grok and OpenAI models
item.description: xAI and OpenAI: A Convovo study reported that, when explicitly forced to recommend a candidate across nearly 500 U.S. midterm races, Grok 4.7 chose Republicans in 92% of its answers and OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol chose Democrats in 97%. The findings raise questions about model behavior and political neutrality, but the article cautions that the test used APIs and an unusually direct prompt, not ordinary chatbot use.

item.title: Block introduces Dessa, a locally runnable full-duplex speech model
item.description: Block: Block introduced Dessa, a full-duplex speech model trained entirely on human speech that can run locally on a consumer computer such as a MacBook M4 Max. The release points toward more natural, on-device voice AI, while Block is seeking safety testing before broader access.

item.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner on AI safety and security
item.description: OpenAI: OpenAI announced a partnership with Poland’s NASK focused on AI safety, security, and technical research. The collaboration is intended to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem; it was published before the monitoring start date.

item.title: Google DeepMind releases a global map of forest types
item.description: Google DeepMind: Google DeepMind and Google Research, working with the World Resources Institute and IIASA, released Forest Typology 2020, a global 10-meter-resolution map distinguishing six forest and land-use types. They also shared an early time series tracking changes from 2017 to 2025, including natural forests converted to plantations or farms.
